Package org.apache.juneau.console.freemarker

Class PageSpec

java.lang.Object
org.apache.juneau.console.freemarker.PageSpec
public final class PageSpec extends Object
Java description of one console page: the active tab, toolkits, page CSS and init scripts, per-request header fields, the stock theme by name, and the page's cards (tables, html and registered custom types) and body attributes.

A PageSpec renders nothing itself. Its values are seeded into the request's PageCapture before any directive runs, so a built page goes through the same <@console> chrome and emits the same #juneau-page contract and the same toolkit asset tags as an FTL page. Chrome (brand, nav tree, footer, theme tokens) stays in the app's chrome template.

Example:

var spec = PageSpec.create() .title("SLO") .tab("slo") .toolkit("views") .css("/css/slo.css") .csrf(token, "X-CSRF") .html("intro", "<p>Queue health</p>") .table(sloTable);

Example:

return PageSpec.create() .tab("changes") .table(ChangesView.def(), c -> c.title("Changes")) .table(TasksView.def(), c -> c.title("Tasks for the selected change") .subscribes(Subscription.to(Topics.selection("changes")).as("params").map("changeId", "ids.0"))) .card(ChartDef.bar("byOwner").title("Open changes by owner").src("/rest/changes/by-owner?q={q}") .x("owner").series("open", "Open").toCardSpec() .subscribes(Subscription.to(Topics.filter("changes")).as("params").map("q", "search"))) .view(req);

Since:
10.0.0

    • htmlSrc

      public PageSpec htmlSrc(String id, String title, String src, boolean sanitize)
      Adds an html card whose body is fetched from src, with a title, optionally rebuilt through the views attribute-allowlist sanitizer. The equivalent of <@card type="html" src="..." sanitize=true>.
      Trust boundary:

      With sanitize false the shell fetches src and inserts the returned HTML as-is through a raw HTML-sink assignment, unsanitized, the same trust level as footer.text (see HtmlCardType). The endpoint must therefore be a trusted first-party route, must never be derived from request data, and must escape any data it embeds in the fragment. src must be a same-origin path; an absolute URL, a scheme, //, .. or a backslash is refused when the page is built, exactly as for every other card.

      With sanitize true the fragment is rebuilt through the views attribute-allowlist sanitizer instead: script, on* handlers, javascript: and data: URLs and every attribute off the allowlist are dropped, and benign markup (text, tables, links, images) survives. It needs the views toolkit on the page; without the toolkit nothing is painted (the shell fails closed rather than inserting the fragment unsanitized). The sanitizer does not remove the need to escape any data you embed in the fragment. Turn it on when the fragment's content is not fully under your control (it embeds user-supplied or third-party markup, or comes from an endpoint you do not own); leave it off for a fragment that needs class, id, style, forms, SVG or iframes, which the allowlist drops. The default stays off.

      Parameters:
      id - The card id.
      title - The card title. May be null for no title.
      src - The same-origin path of the HTML fragment endpoint. Must not be blank.
      sanitize - Whether to rebuild the fetched fragment through the sanitizer.
      Returns:
      This object.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - If src is null or blank.

    • card

      public PageSpec card(CardSpec card)
      Adds a custom-type card with no inline markup.

      When the page renders, a card of an adopter type (any type that is not reserved) is built as <@card> builds it: its body map is the authored body, the type's registered CardTypeHandler validates it and returns the fragment the card carries, and an invalid body fails the render with the <@card> message. An unregistered type takes the generic passthrough, so its body map is carried as-is.

      Parameters:
      card - The card. Its type must not be a removed type or one with a dedicated method.
      Returns:
      This object.

    • card

      public PageSpec card(CardSpec card, String markupOrNull)
      Adds a custom-type card that also takes inline markup.
      Parameters:
      card - The card. See card(CardSpec).
      markupOrNull - The markup, or null. For an adopter type it is the card's body, as the content of <@card> is: the handler parses it (JSON5) or captures it as <template data-card=card.id()>, and subscribes / publishes keys in JSON5 markup are wired onto the card. A card takes at most one of a body map, non-blank markup, template or src.
      Returns:
      This object.

    • dashboard

      public PageSpec dashboard(DashboardSpec dashboard)
      Adds the page's dashboard: a rail of filter sections beside a grid of card panels.

      The panel and card-section cards built by the dashboard are added to this page as ordinary cards, and the dashboard toolkit pack is added (just before charts when that is listed). A by-id panel (panel("notes")) must name a card added before this call, for example with html(String, String).

      Parameters:
      dashboard - The dashboard.
      Returns:
      This object.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - E-77 on any dashboard problem, or if the page already has a dashboard.

    • view

      public FreemarkerView view(RestRequest req)
      Builds the view for this spec.

      The template is template(String) when set, else the ConsoleFreemarkerMixin's chrome template. A built spec is not modified by rendering, so it may be cached and reused across requests. Call spec.view(req) on each request: a reused FreemarkerView would share one adoption flag.

      Parameters:
      req - The current REST request.
      Returns:
      A view for the template, carrying this spec and every attr(String, Object) / header(String, String) passthrough.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - If no template was set and the request has no ConsoleFreemarkerMixin bean.
      IllegalArgumentException - If this spec has no page template and its bus wiring fails R-10 / R-11.
